notes: The deposition, and the cheapest tape in the shelf to write: the
**The witness microphone failed and nobody noticed for an hour**,
which is the in-fiction licence for forty minutes of one lawyer's half
of a conversation. Every answer is a `note` describing its length and
its effect on the room, and the comedy is entirely in the duration.
Two rules held while writing it. Nothing in here tells the audience
who the witness is -- the slate does not name him and counsel never
does, and a Star Trek audience gets there on "expansive" alone. And
nobody wins: counsel does not get the answer, the record does not
improve, and the tape runs out mid-sentence.
The one short line in it -- nine seconds, the shortest answer of the
day, to "where is the latinum now" -- is the only place the tape
suggests the witness is in complete control of the proceeding.
title: Deposition: in the matter of a quantity of latinum
subtitle: Bajoran sector civil claims, witness track failed
author: court recording; witness responses not captured
extra: Forty-one minutes. Two thousand words, none of them his.

lines.text: BAJORAN SECTOR CIVIL CLAIMS: DEPOSITION
IN THE MATTER OF A QUANTITY OF LATINUM
WITNESS TRACK FAILED. RESPONSES NOT RECOVERABLE.
The witness microphone failed and nobody checked it.
I have watched this more times than the talent night.
Please state your name and residence for the record.
A long answer. The stenographer stops partway through.
The name on its own is sufficient. Thank you.
You understand that you remain under oath.
He understands.
I direct your attention to the deposit made in 2367.
Eleven minutes.
I am going to interrupt. That was not the question.
Did you at any point hold the latinum in question?
Four minutes. Counsel's pen stops moving entirely.
Is that a yes.
It is not clear that it is a yes.
Let the record reflect the witness is being expansive.
RECESS
Back on the record. We were at the 2367 deposit.
He starts again from an earlier point than before.
Sir. Sir. We have covered your brother-in-law.
Twice. We have covered him twice now.
A third time. It is longer than either of the others.
Objection. I am objecting to my own witness.
SECOND RECESS
One question. Where is the latinum now.
Nine seconds. The shortest answer of the day.
...I see. And you have nothing further to add.
He has a great deal further to add.
Twenty-two minutes. The tape ends mid-sentence.
RECORDING ENDS
Forty-one minutes. Not one word of it is his.
Somebody in that room knew where it went. Not counsel.
